posts.name: Sovit
posts.cooked:
Dear Sir,

I’ve been facing some issues with the cloud VM we’ve been provided over the past few days. I usually use tmux to manage my workflow—opening a file for editing in one pane while performing tasks like evaluating scripts, reading man or info pages, and navigating with ranger in other panes and windows. This setup worked perfectly fine until last month.

However, I’ve recently noticed that when I have more than one window (or more than two panes) open in tmux, I am sometimes unable to open man pages, while other times it works fine.

image1920×1080 236 KB

Additionally, I’ve been encountering other similar issues over the past few days.

This morning, I ran into another problem while working on BPT4_problem_1. My setup involved a tmux session with vim open in the left pane (to edit my script) and the right pane for running synchro eval to evaluate my score. Every time I ran synchro eval, all the public test cases passed, but every single private test case failed. However, after I closed tmux and reran synchro eval without modifying my script, both public and private test cases passed.

ss1920×1080 119 KB

image1920×1080 96.1 KB

Could this be happening due to resource limitations on the VM? If so, I find it odd since I’ve been using this cloud VM for a while without such issues.

Thank you for your time and guidance.

Best regards

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
Hello,

yes inability to fork is due to the the hard restriction on the total number of processes per user. This has been applied since the fork bomb last month. If you are opening too many processes, you would not be able to open more. However the limit is 40, which should be sufficient even when using tmux. I suspect you have previous sessions as well in your tmux. Try to do tmux a to to attach to a previous session and close them, or alternatively go to kill my process to kill all your processes.

posts.name: Sovit
posts.cooked: I always open only one session at time and if there are other sessions running in the background I always close them. So this might not be the issue here.

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
I just tested it out and it seems that just having two panes in tmux prohibits the private test case running process from forking. Will discuss this with the dev team and get back with a reply or solution.

Thanks for pointing it out.

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
UPDATE: We have slightly increased the limits, so that a tmux window with two panes, one with vim and another with synchro eval should work fine and not give any forking issues. Even tried with two vim and one synchro, works fine. Please log out of all sessions, log back in, and try again and let us know.

Once again, thanks for pointing this out. Cheers!

posts.name: Sovit
posts.cooked: Tested. Increasing max user processes indeed fixed the issue. Thanks for your support!
